title: U.S. House · Maryland's 3rd District
area: Parts of Anne Arundel, Howard, Baltimore and Montgomery counties, including Annapolis and Columbia.

context.text: Incumbent Sarah Elfreth defeated Jennifer Cross, Austin Dyches, Sean Hammond and Robert Morrison in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Bernard Flowers defeated Ray Bly, Felix Seier and John White in the Republican primary.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Maryland, 2026

summary.text: Sarah Elfreth is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 3rd Congressional District. She previously served six years in the Maryland Senate, where she passed 84 bills into law.

background.text: Born in New Jersey in 1988; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Towson University and a master's in public policy from Johns Hopkins University.
Worked as government affairs director with the National Aquarium and as an adjunct professor at Towson University's Honors College.
Served in the Maryland Senate from 2019 to 2025, becoming the youngest woman elected to the chamber in state history.

priorities.text: Protecting reproductive health care access, saying decisions should be between a patient and their doctor.
Gun violence prevention, citing her record passing Maryland laws on public carry, ghost guns and safe storage.
Environmental protection, particularly restoring the Chesapeake Bay and addressing climate change.

positions.summary: Says healthcare decisions belong between a patient and their doctor, voted in the Maryland Senate to expand access to reproductive health care, and co-sponsored a state constitutional amendment on reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: Sarah knows healthcare decisions are between you and your doctor – not elected officials or judges.

positions.summary: Helped pass Maryland laws prohibiting carrying firearms in places like schools and restaurants, banning ghost guns, increasing penalties for illegal possession, and requiring safe storage; says she will push to ban assault weapons and expand background checks in Congress.
Says she passed state laws to invest in clean energy jobs and will fight for climate justice and a faster transition to clean energy in Congress.

record.text: Passed 84 bills into law during five years in the Maryland Senate, on issues including Chesapeake Bay protection, prenatal care expansion and veterans' PTSD care.
Served on the Maryland Senate budget committee overseeing tens of billions of dollars in transportation, environmental and public safety spending.
Serves on the House Natural Resources Committee and House Armed Services Committee for the 2025-2026 term.

summary.text: Bernard Flowers is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 3rd Congressional District, a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel with nearly 21 years of active-duty service.

background.text: Born in Lumberton, North Carolina; served in the U.S. Air Force from 1987 to 2008, including an assignment at the Pentagon on September 11, 2001.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina at Pembroke, a graduate degree from Golden Gate University, and graduated from the U.S. Air Force War College.
After military service, worked in banking and later as a DoD civil servant helping stand up U.S. Cyber Command and serving as a senior technical advisor to NORAD and U.S. Northern Command.

priorities.text: National defense, citing his 21 years of active duty and 13 years as a senior civil servant.
Empowering parents and promoting what he calls excellence in education rather than indoctrination.
Immigration reform, middle-class affordability, fiscal reform, term limits and infrastructure renewal.

positions.summary: Says he wants to depoliticize public schools and empower parents, teachers and local communities in education decisions.
